instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: No Tie Stands
cards.instruction: Turn every even outcome into a formal rematch with a new rule and a consequence for losing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our cakes tied. Next round: one-handed icing. Loser cleans the kitchen. Keep your other hand behind your back, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We could just share the prize.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's distributing it, not deciding it. I'll time the icing; finish means the whole top is covered.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no icing left. We used it all.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then wash our mixing bowls one-handed. First grease-free bowl wins; loser dries both. Please wait for my inspection before you call yours finished.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've split the dinner bill exactly. Now we count backwards from a hundred; first mistake pays the tip. I'll keep score.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll just pay half the tip too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we're tied again. Please choose a deciding test, not another equal payment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We both know how to count. We'll be here all night.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then go down in sevens. No restarting; hesitation counts as a mistake. Say whether you accept those terms before I begin.

cards.title: Every Loss Builds the Comeback
cards.instruction: Treat each setback as proof that the eventual victory will be more impressive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the records of all six losses. Our eventual win will look better with a properly documented starting point.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The tournament's over. I was going to clear the team folder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Archive it, don't clear it. Put next season on a new page; the gap will show how far we came back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The team's disbanding. There won't be a next season.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Call the new page 'reunion'. Please keep everyone's contact details with the scores; winning after we get them back together will be worth the extra chapter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Photograph the collapsed cake before we clear it. Tomorrow's winning one needs an accurate before picture.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The oven's burnt out. You can't bake another here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then label the photograph 'equipment failure' as well. Please capture the oven display; a comeback from both will be much more impressive.

beats.text: The neighbor will lend us her oven, but only from midnight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Confirm the exact time and preheating, please. Keep the message with the photos. When we win, I want the judges to know we began at midnight, not after breakfast.

cards.title: Congratulate Through Your Teeth
cards.instruction: Perform warm praise while allowing competitive resentment to intensify beneath every compliment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Congratulations on the pottery prize. Turn the handle toward the photographer; that side is genuinely lovely.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The judges liked the whole mug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Please support the base while you lift it; they were wonderfully relaxed about that crack.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They called the crack deliberate. It's part of the design.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How bold. Keep their comment beside it at the exhibition, please. I'd hate anyone to mistake your award-winning design for the fault I repaired in mine.

beats.text: Congratulations on the promotion. I'll show you how to chair the meeting; it's lovely they're giving you room to learn.

cards.title: Nothing Without Stakes
cards.instruction: Price every request and decision with a reward, penalty, bargain, or trade.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll lend you the ladder for first choice at the barbecue. Confirm the food part before you take it, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't it just be a favor between friends?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A favor is an advance, not a cancellation. What will you do when I need one?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hold the ladder when you paint your gutter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One full afternoon, then. Please don't put 'hold ladder' down without a duration. I'll trade this weekend's loan for that; agreed?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll apologize for arriving late if you apologize for starting dinner without me. Let's agree the exchange before either of us begins.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd settle for ending the argument.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then specify what ends: no late-arrival jokes for the rest of the evening. My apology has to buy that much.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you stop bringing up the cold food.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Matched terms. Say 'for the evening', please; I won't trade an all-night promise for a pause until dessert. Then we can apologize together.

cards.title: Fair Means I Can Win
cards.instruction: Agree to any rule or bargain only after interpreting fairness in a way that preserves your advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll race if we compensate for tired legs. Move my start forward; I've been carrying boxes upstairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've all had a tiring morning. Same line for everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then allow recovery time proportionally. Carrying upstairs isn't the same as sitting in traffic; please account for the difference.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. Everyone gets five minutes' rest before we start.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. Then measure my head start after the rest. Five minutes compensates the tiredness; it doesn't cancel the stairs. Please keep those adjustments separate.
